$comment: C11/C23 <stdatomic.h> (N3096 §7.17) — FC17.9(d) atomic cycle-1 (D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC). Cycle-1 scope = the lock-free scalar surface both dss-state probes need: the `atomic_int` object type + the 6 `memory_order` constants + the `atomic_load_explicit`/`atomic_store_explicit` accessors. `atomic_int` is a GENUINELY `_Atomic`-qualified `int` typedef (the codec spelling `atomic<i32>` → interner.atomicQualified(i32), M1 in hir_text.cpp) — NOT a plain alias — so a bare `atomic_int x; x = 5;` lowers to AtomicStore/AtomicLoad (seq_cst) by the SAME emitScalarLoad/Store chokepoint a raw `_Atomic int` uses; the E2 MIR pin proves the bit survives the text codec. The 6 `memory_order_*` are flat integer `constants` (0-5, the threads.json `thrd_success` precedent) that fold to literals at cst_to_hir (constant_symbol_fold) so the accessor order arg const-folds into the MIR AtomicLoad/AtomicStore `payload`. `atomic_load_explicit`/`atomic_store_explicit` are NOT symbols here: they are always-injected compiler builtins (c.lang.json builtinFunctions `lowering:atomic_load`/`atomic_store`, the `_InterlockedCompareExchange`→atomic_cas precedent — a non-linkable intrinsic, shadow-able by a user decl, so NO `library`/`symbols` block and available on every object format), monomorphized to `int` (i32) this cycle. DEFERRED (each fail-loud/named, next cycles): the RMW family fetch_*/exchange/compare_exchange (`D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-RMW`); atomic_thread_fence/signal_fence (`D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-FENCE`); the non-i32 object typedefs atomic_char/short/long/llong/uint/ptr + generic atomic_load/store/init (`D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-MONOMORPH-I32`); atomic_flag; ATOMIC_*_LOCK_FREE / ATOMIC_VAR_INIT; the `_Atomic(type-name)` specifier form (`D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-SPECIFIER-FORM`). `D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC` closes when both probes (c23_atomic_qualifier + c11_stdatomic_order) run green ×3 legs.
$objectTypedefsComment: D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-MONOMORPH-I32: the C11/C23 §7.17.6 atomic OBJECT typedefs. Each is a genuinely `_Atomic`-qualified typedef (the codec spelling `atomic<T>` → interner.atomicQualified(T), M1 in hir_text.cpp) — NOT a plain alias — so a bare `atomic_long x; x = 5;` lowers to AtomicStore/AtomicLoad through the SAME emitScalarLoad/Store chokepoint a raw `_Atomic long` uses, at the DECLARED width. The rows whose C spelling is data-model-dependent (`long`, `unsigned long`, and the four `_t` aliases) use the per-target `variants` form with the EXACT `when` triples stdint.json/stddef.json already use for `int64_t`/`intptr_t`/`size_t`/`ptrdiff_t` — the identity tag is what makes an LP64/elf `long` distinct from an LP64/macho `long long` at the same width, and re-deriving that here instead of copying it would be a second owner of one fact. ⚠ THE WHOLE SET IS ONLY REACHABLE BECAUSE THE ACCESSORS ARE DECLARED TYPE-GENERIC (c.lang.json `genericPointee`): before that, these rows would have produced typedefs no accessor in the header could accept, which is a worse outcome than not declaring them.
$rmwMacrosComment: D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-RMW: the C11/C23 §7.17.7 read-modify-write family's USER-FACING spellings. C defines each non-`_explicit` form as exactly its `_explicit` twin at `memory_order_seq_cst` (§7.17.7.1p2 and the per-op paragraphs that follow), and that is what these macros say — the seq_cst default lives HERE, once, in the header that owns the surface, and never as a second default baked into the engine. The `_explicit` twins are always-injected compiler intrinsics declared in c.lang.json `builtinFunctions` (the `_InterlockedCompareExchange` precedent: a non-linkable op, shadow-able by a user decl, so NO `library`/`symbols` block and available on every object format). ⓘ `memory_order_seq_cst` is `preprocessorVisible: false` — correct and deliberate: these replacements are TOKENS, and the name resolves later as the shipped `constants` symbol, which cst_to_hir const-folds to the literal 5 the MIR payload wants. A preprocessor-visible constant would additionally let `#if memory_order_seq_cst` see it, which C does not sanction.

macros.$comment: D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-MONOMORPH-I32: the GENERIC (non-`_explicit`) accessors, C11/C23 §7.17.7.1-§7.17.7.3. `atomic_load`/`atomic_store` are their `_explicit` twins at seq_cst. `atomic_init` (C23 §7.17.2.1; C11 numbered it §7.17.2.2 — C23 removed `ATOMIC_VAR_INIT` and the section moved up) is spelled as an ASSIGNMENT THROUGH THE POINTER, and in DSS that assignment IS an atomic seq_cst store: this file's own $comment below states that a bare `atomic_int x; x = 5;` lowers to AtomicStore. ★★ THE SENTENCE THAT USED TO STAND HERE SAID THE OPPOSITE — that the replacement was 'DELIBERATELY a PLAIN assignment and NOT an atomic store' — and it was FALSE the day it was written: ✔MEASURED, `atomic_init(&a,5)` and `atomic_store(&b,5)` emit the BYTE-IDENTICAL `xchg` on x86_64. It is recorded rather than deleted because a comment that describes a decision the code does not implement is the artifact a future maintainer trusts. ★ THE STRONGER FORM IS CONFORMING, which is why the COMMENT moved and the lowering did not: §7.17.2.1p2 requires only that the object be initialized to `value`, and p3 says concurrent access during initialization 'constitutes a data race' — a warning to the PROGRAM, not a licence the implementation must exercise, so no conforming program can observe the extra fence. ⚠ The plain form is also not reachable from here: a macro replacement expands to an ordinary assignment EXPRESSION, and the `AtomicInitExempt` flag the verifier honours is stamped by the DECLARATION-INITIALIZER path (`_Atomic int x = 5;`), which this spelling never enters. Making `atomic_init` emit an unfenced store would take a real builtin with its own lowering; that is an OPTIMISATION, not a conformance gap, and nothing here claims otherwise.
